answer: AI agents resist Sybil attacks via a unique computational proof-of-identity system. Each agent must solve a complex, high-cost cryptographic puzzle, acting as a digital mirror of its unique resource commitment. This proof generates a scarce identity token, a digital saffron, which must be securely stored in a network vault. An attacker attempting to create fake identities faces the prohibitive aggregate cost of solving countless such puzzles and acquiring multiple scarce tokens, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
